issues.description: Command names disagree with the rest of the command vocabulary in the same file
issues.detail: The existing commands are `quickmark_save`, `quickmark_load`, `bookmark_add`, `bookmark_load` — singular noun, underscore-separated. The new ones are `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` — plural. The feature file then writes them as `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload`. An author who has reasoned about his naming does not introduce a new pluralization rule in the same file as a side effect of a four-line patch. Pick a convention and obey it.

issues.description: Constructor postcondition silently changed: `reload()` now emits `changed` during `__init__`
issues.detail: Previously `__init__` populated `marks` without emitting `changed`. The refactor routes initialisation through `reload()`, which now emits `changed` before `_init_savemanager` has run and before any external observer can plausibly be connected. The frame of `__init__` has been altered without anyone stating it. Either suppress the signal during construction or document that the first `changed` is fired from the constructor.

issues.description: No invariant stated for `reload()` on failure; partial state is reachable
issues.detail: `reload()` clears `marks`, emits no intermediate signal, then re-reads the file. If `_init_lineparser` or `_parse_line` raises (malformed line, I/O error, decode error), `marks` is left empty and `changed` is never emitted, yet the on-disk file is intact. The precondition/postcondition pair is unstated and the observable state diverges from disk. Build the new dict first; swap atomically; emit once.

issues.description: Test does not exercise the QuickmarkManager path, only BookmarkManager
issues.detail: `test_reload` covers `BookmarkManager.reload()`. `QuickmarkManager` inherits the same method but overrides `_parse_line` and reads a different file. The end2end scenarios are a thin smoke test of the message string. No unit test demonstrates that quickmark reload actually replaces entries. Tests show the presence of bugs, not their absence — and here they are not even being asked.

issues.description: End-to-end scenarios are unnamed and assert only the user-visible message
issues.detail: Both new `Scenario:` blocks lack titles and only check that the info message appears. They prove the command is wired and prints a string; they do not prove that the in-memory marks were actually replaced by the on-disk contents. Name the scenario, mutate the file on disk between writes, and assert the resulting marks — otherwise the test is decorative.

issues.description: Unreasoned interaction with the save manager: reload races with autosave
issues.detail: `UrlMarkManager` registers a `save-manager` entry whose dirty flag is driven by the same `changed` signal. `reload()` emits `changed`, which will mark the manager dirty and schedule a save of the just-loaded contents back to the same file. The author has not stated whether this is intended; at minimum the round-trip should be reasoned about and stated, not discovered later in an issue report.

review.summary: A modest, mostly mechanical patch that lifts initialisation into a `reload()` method and exposes it as two commands. The mechanical part is fine; the reasoning around it is absent. The author has not stated the precondition or postcondition of `reload()`, has not considered failure mid-reload, has not noticed that `__init__` now emits `changed`, and has not reckoned with the autosave round-trip the new signal will provoke. Naming drifts from singular to plural within the same file without comment, and the tests demonstrate only that a string appears on screen — TESTED-NOT-PROVED. Verdict: UNREASONED but salvageable. State the spec, build-then-swap inside `reload()`, cover the quickmark path, and align the command names.
